title: Lighthouse & Beta Launch Readiness Playbook for Customer Onboarding
creator: Nora Patel
description: Goal: Prepare a small, controlled customer launch (beta + 3 lighthouse accounts) for the Private and Dedicated offerings with clear success criteria, a tight feedback loop, and coordinated release notes / GTM assets. This playbook organizes cross-team deliverables (Product, Engineering, Design, Security, Support, Solutions), signoffs, and the timeline to go from internal alpha to an externally communicated beta. It includes the technical readiness checklist, customer-facing comms, escalation paths, and post-beta evaluation steps. The scope intentionally excludes full public self-serve launch; this ticket focuses on targeted customer onboarding and capture of qualitative + quantitative feedback to validate unit economics and operational runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 3 lighthouse customers onboarded and actively sending traffic for at least two workload patterns (inference bursts and steady throughput). 2) Release notes drafted, reviewed by Legal and Security, and published to customer portal at beta start. 3) Instrumentation and dashboards show baseline metrics (p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, error rate, cache hit rate). 4) Feedback loop established with weekly readouts and documented action items. 5) Post-beta report with recommendations accepted by PM and Eng leads.
success_criteria: Quantitative: p95 inference latency <= SLA target (per-account SLO), error rate < 0.5% for beta traffic, cost per 1k tokens within 15% of projected. Qualitative: >=2 lighthouse customers confirm product fit and provide prioritized feature requests; support satisfaction score >= 4/5 on onboarding surveys.
tasks: Finalize beta cohort selection and NDAs with legal
Complete private deployment runbook and rollback procedure
Instrumentation: add per-account tracing and cost tagging
Create onboarding checklist and customer success playbook
Draft release notes and coordinate Legal/Sec review
Design in-console banners + opt-in flow for beta accounts
Prepare support SLAs and escalation matrix
Schedule weekly beta readout and feedback synthesis
timeline_summary: Week 0-1: finalize cohort and legal; Week 2: finish infra hardening, add instrumentation; Week 3: internal dry-run with internal product users; Week 4: lighthouse onboarding begins; Weeks 5-8: active beta, weekly readouts; Week 9: post-beta analysis and decision on expansion.
rollout_plan: Start with 3 lighthouse accounts (invited) + 10 small alpha customers. Staged ramp: 10% traffic for week 1, 50% week 2, full beta traffic week 3 after green-light. Fallback: automatic routing to hosted-compatible model variants if dedicated capacity saturation detected. Communication cadence: welcome email + onboarding call, daily sync first 72 hours, weekly product readout.
feedback_loop: Primary channel: dedicated Slack workspace + weekly 60-min readout. Feedback is triaged into Product backlog, Engineering bugs, and Docs/Support actions within 48 hours. All customer-reported regressions tied to a ticket with severity and customer impact. We will run two synthetic prompt suites daily to detect regressions and compare against baseline outputs; any drift >5% in quality metrics triggers immediate investigation.
release_notes_coordination: Owner: PM (Ethan). Steps: 1) Draft notes using release-notes template. 2) Attach 'Known limitations' for private deployments and beta constraints. 3) Legal/Security review window = 48 hours. 4) Engineering signoff on any compatibility caveats. 5) Publish to customer portal and notify lighthouse accounts 24 hours prior. Include sample prompts, expected responses, and migration guidance.
risks_mitigations:
Risk: Dedicated capacity contention leading to degraded latency. Mitigation: pre-reserve burst capacity + automated fallback to compatible model.
Risk: Sensitive customer data in logs. Mitigation: ensure KMS/HSM integration and mask logs per privacy guidelines.
Risk: Slow feedback loop. Mitigation: mandatory 48-hour triage SLA and weekly feedback synthesis owned by Solutions.
